passages.text: Now the sons of the prophets said to Elisha, “Please take note that the place where we meet with you is too small for us.
passages.sermon: The sons of the prophets spoke to Elisha.\r\nThey said, “Elisha, we meet with you in this place.\r\nThis place is too small for us.”
passages.original: וַיֹּאמְר֥וּ בְנֵֽי־ הַנְּבִיאִ֖ים אֶל־ אֱלִישָׁ֑ע הִנֵּֽה־ נָ֣א הַמָּק֗וֹם אֲשֶׁ֨ר אֲנַ֜חְנוּ יֹשְׁבִ֥ים שָׁ֛ם לְפָנֶ֖יךָ צַ֥ר מִמֶּֽנּוּ׃

passages.text: Please let us go to the Jordan, where each of us can get a log so we can build ourselves a place to live there.” “Go,” said Elisha.
passages.sermon:
The sons of the prophets spoke to Elisha.
They said, “Let us go to the Jordan River.
Each of us will take a log from there.
We will build a place for ourselves to live there.”
Elisha said, “Go.”
passages.original: נֵֽלֲכָה־ נָּ֣א עַד־ הַיַּרְדֵּ֗ן וְנִקְחָ֤ה מִשָּׁם֙ אִ֚ישׁ קוֹרָ֣ה אֶחָ֔ת וְנַעֲשֶׂה־ לָּ֥נוּ שָׁ֛ם מָק֖וֹם לָשֶׁ֣בֶת שָׁ֑ם וַיֹּ֖אמֶר לֵֽכוּ׃

passages.text: Then one of them said, “Please come with your servants.” “I will come,” he replied.
passages.sermon:
One of the sons of the prophets spoke to Elisha.
He said, “Please come with your servants.”
Elisha answered him.
He said, “I will come.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ הָֽאֶחָ֔ד ה֥וֹאֶל נָ֖א וְלֵ֣ךְ אֶת־ עֲבָדֶ֑יךָ וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אֲנִ֥י אֵלֵֽךְ׃

passages.text: So Elisha went with them, and when they came to the Jordan, they began to cut down some trees.
passages.sermon:
Elisha was a prophet of God.
Elisha went with the group of men.
They all traveled to the Jordan River.
When they arrived at the Jordan River, they began to cut down trees.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֖לֶךְ אִתָּ֑ם וַיָּבֹ֙אוּ֙ הַיַּרְדֵּ֔נָה וַֽיִּגְזְר֖וּ הָעֵצִֽים׃

passages.text: As one of them was cutting down a tree, the iron axe head fell into the water. “Oh, my master,” he cried out, “it was borrowed!”
passages.sermon:
One man was cutting down a tree.
He used an axe.
The iron axe head fell into the water.
He cried out loudly.
He said, “Oh, my master!”
He said, “The axe was borrowed.”
passages.original: וַיְהִ֤י הָֽאֶחָד֙ מַפִּ֣יל הַקּוֹרָ֔ה וְאֶת־ הַבַּרְזֶ֖ל נָפַ֣ל אֶל־ הַמָּ֑יִם וַיִּצְעַ֥ק וַיֹּ֛אמֶר אֲהָ֥הּ אֲדֹנִ֖י וְה֥וּא שָׁאֽוּל׃

passages.text: “Where did it fall?” asked the man of God. And when he showed him the place, the man of God cut a stick, threw it there, and made the iron float.
passages.sermon:
The man of God was Elisha.
Elisha asked, “Where did it fall?”
The man showed Elisha the place.
Elisha cut a stick.
Elisha threw the stick to that place.
The iron floated.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר אִישׁ־ הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים אָ֣נָה נָפָ֑ל וַיַּרְאֵ֙הוּ֙ אֶת־ הַמָּק֔וֹם וַיִּקְצָב־ עֵץ֙ וַיַּשְׁלֶךְ־ שָׁ֔מָּה וַיָּ֖צֶף הַבַּרְזֶֽל׃

passages.text: “Lift it out,” he said, and the man reached out his hand and took it.
passages.sermon:
The man of God spoke.
He said, “Lift it out.”
The man reached out his hand.
He took the iron axe head.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר הָ֣רֶם לָ֑ךְ וַיִּשְׁלַ֥ח יָד֖וֹ וַיִּקָּחֵֽהוּ׃פ

passages.text: Now the king of Aram was at war against Israel. After consulting with his servants, he said, “My camp will be in such and such a place.”
passages.sermon:
The king of Aram fought against Israel.
He planned war against Israel.
He spoke with his servants.
He said, “I will set up my camp in a certain place.”
passages.original: וּמֶ֣לֶךְ אֲרָ֔ם הָיָ֥ה נִלְחָ֖ם בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיִּוָּעַץ֙ אֶל־ עֲבָדָ֣יו לֵאמֹ֗ר אֶל־ מְק֛וֹם פְּלֹנִ֥י אַלְמֹנִ֖י תַּחֲנֹתִֽי׃

passages.text: Then the man of God sent word to the king of Israel: “Be careful passing by this place, for the Arameans are going down there.”
passages.sermon:
Elisha was a prophet in Israel.
Elisha was called the man of God.
Elisha sent a message to the king of Israel.
Elisha warned the king.
He said, “Be careful when you pass by this place.
The Arameans are going down there.”
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁלַ֞ח אִ֣ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֗ים אֶל־ מֶ֤לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר הִשָּׁ֕מֶר מֵעֲבֹ֖ר הַמָּק֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה כִּֽי־ שָׁ֖ם אֲרָ֥ם נְחִתִּֽים׃

passages.text: So the king of Israel sent word to the place the man of God had pointed out. Time and again Elisha warned the king, so that he was on his guard in such places.
passages.sermon:
The king of Israel received warnings from Elisha.
Elisha was a prophet and a man of God in Israel.
Elisha told the king about certain places.
The king sent word to those places.
Elisha warned the king many times.
The king stayed alert in those places.
This happened more than once.
This happened more than twice.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁלַ֞ח מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל אֶֽל־ הַמָּק֞וֹם אֲשֶׁ֨ר אָֽמַר־ ל֧וֹ אִישׁ־ הָאֱלֹהִ֛ים וְהִזְהִירָהּ וְנִשְׁמַ֣ר שָׁ֑ם לֹ֥א אַחַ֖ת וְלֹ֥א שְׁתָּֽיִם׃

passages.text: For this reason the king of Aram became enraged and called his servants to demand of them, “Tell me, which one of us is on the side of the king of Israel?”
passages.sermon:
The king of Aram heard what happened.
He became very angry.
He called his servants to him.
He spoke to his servants.
He said, “Tell me this.
Who among us is helping the king of Israel?”
passages.original: וַיִּסָּעֵר֙ לֵ֣ב מֶֽלֶךְ־ אֲרָ֔ם עַל־ הַדָּבָ֖ר הַזֶּ֑ה וַיִּקְרָ֤א אֶל־ עֲבָדָיו֙ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵיהֶ֔ם הֲלוֹא֙ תַּגִּ֣ידוּ לִ֔י מִ֥י מִשֶּׁלָּ֖נוּ אֶל־ מֶ֥לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: But one of his servants replied, “No one, my lord the king. For Elisha, the prophet in Israel, tells the king of Israel the very words you speak in your bedroom.”
passages.sermon:
One of the king’s servants spoke.
He said, “No one among us is a traitor, my lord the king.”
Elisha is a prophet in Israel.
Elisha tells the king of Israel what you say in your bedroom.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ אַחַ֣ד מֵֽעֲבָדָ֔יו ל֖וֹא אֲדֹנִ֣י הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ כִּֽי־ אֱלִישָׁ֤ע הַנָּבִיא֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל יַגִּיד֙ לְמֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֶת־ הַ֨דְּבָרִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר תְּדַבֵּ֖ר בַּחֲדַ֥ר מִשְׁכָּבֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: So the king said, “Go and see where he is, that I may send men to capture him.” On receiving the report, “Elisha is in Dothan,” the king of Aram sent horses, chariots, and a great army. They went there by night and surrounded the city.
passages.sermon:
The king of Aram wanted to capture Elisha.
He spoke to his servants.
He said, “Go and find out where Elisha is.”
He said, “I will send men to seize him.”
The servants brought a report to the king.
They said, “Elisha is in Dothan.”
The king sent horses to Dothan.
He sent chariots to Dothan.
He sent a large army to Dothan.
They arrived at night.
They surrounded the city.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר לְכ֤וּ וּרְאוּ֙ אֵיכֹ֣ה ה֔וּא וְאֶשְׁלַ֖ח וְאֶקָּחֵ֑הוּ וַיֻּגַּד־ ל֥וֹ לֵאמֹ֖ר הִנֵּ֥ה בְדֹתָֽן׃ וַיִּשְׁלַח־ שָׁ֛מָּה סוּסִ֥ים וְרֶ֖כֶב וְחַ֣יִל כָּבֵ֑ד וַיָּבֹ֣אוּ לַ֔יְלָה וַיַּקִּ֖פוּ עַל־ הָעִֽיר׃

passages.text: When the servant of the man of God got up and went out early in the morning, an army with horses and chariots had surrounded the city. So he asked Elisha, “Oh, my master, what are we to do?”
passages.sermon:
Elisha was a prophet in Israel.
He had a servant.
The servant got up early in the morning.
He went outside.
He saw an army around the city.
The army had horses and chariots.
The servant became afraid.
He spoke to Elisha.
He said, “Oh, my master, what are we to do?”
passages.original: וַ֠יַּשְׁכֵּם מְשָׁרֵ֨ת אִ֥ישׁ הָֽאֱלֹהִים֮ לָקוּם֒ וַיֵּצֵ֕א וְהִנֵּה־ חַ֛יִל סוֹבֵ֥ב אֶת־ הָעִ֖יר וְס֣וּס וָרָ֑כֶב וַיֹּ֨אמֶר נַעֲר֥וֹ אֵלָ֛יו אֲהָ֥הּ אֲדֹנִ֖י אֵיכָ֥ה נַֽעֲשֶֽׂה׃

passages.text: “Do not be afraid,” Elisha answered, “for those who are with us are more than those who are with them.”
passages.sermon:
Elisha was a prophet of God.
Elisha spoke to his servant.
Elisha said, “Do not be afraid.”
God is with us.
Those who are with us are many.
Those who are with them are fewer than those with us.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אַל־ תִּירָ֑א כִּ֤י רַבִּים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אִתָּ֔נוּ מֵאֲשֶׁ֖ר אוֹתָֽם׃

passages.text: Then Elisha prayed, “O LORD, please open his eyes that he may see.” And the LORD opened the eyes of the young man, and he saw that the hills were full of horses and chariots of fire all around Elisha.
passages.sermon:
Elisha was a prophet of God.
A young man served Elisha.
The young man could not see God's protection.
Elisha prayed to the LORD.
Elisha said, “LORD, please open his eyes so he may see.”
The LORD opened the young man’s eyes.
The young man saw the hills.
The hills were full of horses and chariots of fire.
The horses and chariots of fire surrounded Elisha.
passages.original: וַיִּתְפַּלֵּ֤ל אֱלִישָׁע֙ וַיֹּאמַ֔ר יְהוָ֕ה פְּקַח־ נָ֥א אֶת־ עֵינָ֖יו וְיִרְאֶ֑ה וַיִּפְקַ֤ח יְהוָה֙ אֶת־ עֵינֵ֣י הַנַּ֔עַר וַיַּ֗רְא וְהִנֵּ֨ה הָהָ֜ר מָלֵ֨א סוּסִ֥ים וְרֶ֛כֶב אֵ֖שׁ סְבִיבֹ֥ת אֱלִישָֽׁע׃

passages.text: As the Arameans came down against him, Elisha prayed to the LORD, “Please strike these people with blindness.” So He struck them with blindness, according to the word of Elisha.
passages.sermon:
The Arameans came down against Elisha.
Elisha was a prophet of God.
Elisha prayed to the LORD.
Elisha said, “Please strike these people with blindness.”
The LORD struck the Arameans with blindness.
The LORD did this as Elisha had asked.
passages.original: וַיֵּרְדוּ֮ אֵלָיו֒ וַיִּתְפַּלֵּ֨ל אֱלִישָׁ֤ע אֶל־ יְהוָה֙ וַיֹּאמַ֔ר הַךְ־ נָ֥א אֶת־ הַגּוֹי־ הַזֶּ֖ה בַּסַּנְוֵרִ֑ים וַיַּכֵּ֥ם בַּסַּנְוֵרִ֖ים כִּדְבַ֥ר אֱלִישָֽׁע׃

passages.text: And Elisha told them, “This is not the way, and this is not the city. Follow me, and I will take you to the man you are seeking.” And he led them to Samaria.
passages.sermon:
Elisha was a prophet of God in Israel.
Elisha spoke to the Aramean soldiers.
He said, “This is not the way.”
He said, “This is not the city.”
He said, “Follow me.”
He said, “I will take you to the man you are seeking.”
Elisha led the soldiers to Samaria.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֜ם אֱלִישָׁ֗ע לֹ֣א זֶ֣ה הַדֶּרֶךְ֮ וְלֹ֣א זֹ֣ה הָעִיר֒ לְכ֣וּ אַחֲרַ֔י וְאוֹלִ֣יכָה אֶתְכֶ֔ם אֶל־ הָאִ֖ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תְּבַקֵּשׁ֑וּן וַיֹּ֥לֶךְ אוֹתָ֖ם שֹׁמְרֽוֹנָה׃

passages.text: When they had entered Samaria, Elisha said, “O LORD, open the eyes of these men that they may see.” Then the LORD opened their eyes, and they looked around and discovered that they were in Samaria.
passages.sermon:
The Aramean soldiers entered Samaria.
Elisha was a prophet of God.
Elisha spoke to the LORD.
Elisha said, “LORD, open the eyes of these men so they may see.”
The LORD opened the eyes of the Aramean soldiers.
The soldiers looked around.
They saw that they were inside Samaria.
passages.original: וַיְהִי֮ כְּבֹאָ֣ם שֹׁמְרוֹן֒ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֱלִישָׁ֔ע יְהוָ֕ה פְּקַ֥ח אֶת־ עֵינֵֽי־ אֵ֖לֶּה וְיִרְא֑וּ וַיִּפְקַ֤ח יְהוָה֙ אֶת־ עֵ֣ינֵיהֶ֔ם וַיִּרְא֕וּ וְהִנֵּ֖ה בְּת֥וֹךְ שֹׁמְרֽוֹן׃

passages.text: And when the king of Israel saw them, he asked Elisha, “My father, shall I kill them? Shall I kill them?”
passages.sermon:
The king of Israel saw the Aramean soldiers.
Elisha was a prophet of God.
The king spoke to Elisha.
The king called Elisha “my father.”
The king asked Elisha a question.
He said, “Shall I kill them?”
He repeated, “Shall I kill them?”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר מֶֽלֶךְ־ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֶל־ אֱלִישָׁ֔ע כִּרְאֹת֖וֹ אוֹתָ֑ם הַאַכֶּ֥ה אַכֶּ֖ה אָבִֽי׃

passages.text: “Do not kill them,” he replied. “Would you kill those you have captured with your own sword or bow? Set food and water before them, that they may eat and drink and then return to their master.”
passages.sermon:
Elisha was a prophet in Israel.
The king of Israel asked Elisha if he should kill the Aramean soldiers.
Elisha answered the king.
Elisha said, "Do not kill them."
Elisha asked, "Would you kill those you have captured with your sword or your bow?"
Elisha told the king, "Set food and water in front of them."
Elisha said, "Let them eat and drink."
Elisha said, "Then let them go back to their master."
passages.original: וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ לֹ֣א תַכֶּ֔ה הַאֲשֶׁ֥ר שָׁבִ֛יתָ בְּחַרְבְּךָ֥ וּֽבְקַשְׁתְּךָ֖ אַתָּ֣ה מַכֶּ֑ה שִׂים֩ לֶ֨חֶם וָמַ֜יִם לִפְנֵיהֶ֗ם וְיֹֽאכְלוּ֙ וְיִשְׁתּ֔וּ וְיֵלְכ֖וּ אֶל־ אֲדֹנֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: So the king prepared a great feast for them, and after they had finished eating and drinking, he sent them away, and they returned to their master. And the Aramean raiders did not come into the land of Israel again.
passages.sermon:
The king of Israel showed mercy to the Aramean soldiers.
He prepared a great feast for them.
The Aramean soldiers ate.
They drank.
After they finished, the king sent them away.
The Aramean soldiers returned to their master.
After this, the Aramean raiders did not come again into the land of Israel.
passages.original: וַיִּכְרֶ֨ה לָהֶ֜ם כֵּרָ֣ה גְדוֹלָ֗ה וַיֹּֽאכְלוּ֙ וַיִּשְׁתּ֔וּ וַֽיְשַׁלְּחֵ֔ם וַיֵּלְכ֖וּ אֶל־ אֲדֹֽנֵיהֶ֑ם וְלֹֽא־ יָ֤סְפוּ עוֹד֙ גְּדוּדֵ֣י אֲרָ֔ם לָב֖וֹא בְּאֶ֥רֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃פ

passages.text: Some time later, Ben-hadad king of Aram assembled his entire army and marched up to besiege Samaria.
passages.sermon:
Ben-hadad was the king of Aram.
He gathered his entire army.
He led them to Samaria.
He surrounded the city.
He began a siege against Samaria.
passages.original: וַֽיְהִי֙ אַחֲרֵי־ כֵ֔ן וַיִּקְבֹּ֛ץ בֶּן־ הֲדַ֥ד מֶֽלֶךְ־ אֲרָ֖ם אֶת־ כָּל־ מַחֲנֵ֑הוּ וַיַּ֕עַל וַיָּ֖צַר עַל־ שֹׁמְרֽוֹן׃

passages.text: So there was a great famine in Samaria. Indeed, they besieged the city so long that a donkey’s head sold for eighty shekels of silver, and a quarter cab of dove’s dung sold for five shekels of silver.
passages.sermon:
There was a great famine in Samaria.
Enemy soldiers surrounded the city for a long time.
Food became very scarce.
A donkey’s head sold for eighty shekels of silver.
A quarter of a cab of dove’s dung sold for five shekels of silver.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֨י רָעָ֤ב גָּדוֹל֙ בְּשֹׁ֣מְר֔וֹן וְהִנֵּ֖ה צָרִ֣ים עָלֶ֑יהָ עַ֣ד הֱי֤וֹת רֹאשׁ־ חֲמוֹר֙ בִּשְׁמֹנִ֣ים כֶּ֔סֶף וְרֹ֛בַע הַקַּ֥ב חֲרֵייוֹנִים בַּחֲמִשָּׁה־ כָֽסֶף׃

passages.text: As the king of Israel was passing by on the wall, a woman cried out to him, “Help me, my lord the king!”
passages.sermon:
The king of Israel walked along the city wall.
A woman saw the king.
She called out to him.
She said, “Help me, my lord the king!”
passages.original: וַֽיְהִי֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל עֹבֵ֖ר עַל־ הַחֹמָ֑ה וְאִשָּׁ֗ה צָעֲקָ֤ה אֵלָיו֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר הוֹשִׁ֖יעָה אֲדֹנִ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

passages.text: He answered, “If the LORD does not help you, where can I find help for you? From the threshing floor or the winepress?”
passages.sermon:
The king of Israel spoke to the woman.
He said, “If the LORD does not help you, I cannot help you.
I have nothing to give you.
I have nothing from the threshing floor.
I have nothing from the winepress.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ אַל־ יוֹשִׁעֵ֣ךְ יְהוָ֔ה מֵאַ֖יִן אֽוֹשִׁיעֵ֑ךְ הֲמִן־ הַגֹּ֖רֶן א֥וֹ מִן־ הַיָּֽקֶב׃

passages.text: Then the king asked her, “What is the matter?” And she answered, “This woman said to me, ‘Give up your son, that we may eat him, and tomorrow we will eat my son.’
passages.sermon:
The king of Israel was passing by on the wall.
A woman cried out to him for help.
The king asked the woman, “What is the matter?”
The woman answered the king.
She said, “This woman said to me, ‘Give up your son today.
We will eat him today.
Tomorrow we will eat my son.’”
passages.original: וַיֹּֽאמֶר־ לָ֥הּ הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ מַה־ לָּ֑ךְ וַתֹּ֗אמֶר הָאִשָּׁ֨ה הַזֹּ֜את אָמְרָ֣ה אֵלַ֗י תְּנִ֤י אֶת־ בְּנֵךְ֙ וְנֹאכְלֶ֣נּוּ הַיּ֔וֹם וְאֶת־ בְּנִ֖י נֹאכַ֥ל מָחָֽר׃

passages.text: So we boiled my son and ate him, and the next day I said to her, ‘Give up your son, that we may eat him.’ But she had hidden her son.”
passages.sermon:
A woman spoke to the king of Israel during a famine in Samaria.
She said, “We boiled my son.
We ate him.
The next day, I spoke to the other woman.
I said, ‘Give your son.
We will eat him.’
But she hid her son.”
passages.original: וַנְּבַשֵּׁ֥ל אֶת־ בְּנִ֖י וַנֹּֽאכְלֵ֑הוּ וָאֹמַ֨ר אֵלֶ֜יהָ בַּיּ֣וֹם הָאַחֵ֗ר תְּנִ֤י אֶת־ בְּנֵךְ֙ וְנֹ֣אכְלֶ֔נּוּ וַתַּחְבִּ֖א אֶת־ בְּנָֽהּ׃

passages.text: When the king heard the words of the woman, he tore his clothes. And as he passed by on the wall, the people saw the sackcloth under his clothes next to his skin.
passages.sermon:
The king of Israel heard the woman’s words.
He tore his clothes.
He walked along the city wall.
The people saw him.
They saw sackcloth under his clothes.
The sackcloth was next to his skin.
passages.original: וַיְהִי֩ כִשְׁמֹ֨עַ הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ אֶת־ דִּבְרֵ֤י הָֽאִשָּׁה֙ וַיִּקְרַ֣ע אֶת־ בְּגָדָ֔יו וְה֖וּא עֹבֵ֣ר עַל־ הַחֹמָ֑ה וַיַּ֣רְא הָעָ֔ם וְהִנֵּ֥ה הַשַּׂ֛ק עַל־ בְּשָׂר֖וֹ מִבָּֽיִת׃

passages.text: He announced, “May God punish me, and ever so severely, if the head of Elisha son of Shaphat remains on his shoulders through this day!”
passages.sermon:
The king of Israel heard the woman’s words.
He became very angry.
He spoke a vow.
He said, “May God punish me.”
He said, “May God punish me even more if I do not act.”
He said, “Elisha is the son of Shaphat.”
He said, “Elisha’s head will not remain on his shoulders today.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר כֹּֽה־ יַעֲשֶׂה־ לִּ֥י אֱלֹהִ֖ים וְכֹ֣ה יוֹסִ֑ף אִֽם־ יַעֲמֹ֞ד רֹ֣אשׁ אֱלִישָׁ֧ע בֶּן־ שָׁפָ֛ט עָלָ֖יו הַיּֽוֹם׃

passages.text: Now Elisha was sitting in his house, and the elders were sitting with him. The king sent a messenger ahead, but before he arrived, Elisha said to the elders, “Do you see how this murderer has sent someone to cut off my head? Look, when the messenger comes, shut the door to keep him out. Is not the sound of his master’s footsteps behind him?”
passages.sermon:
Elisha was a prophet of God.
Elisha sat in his house.
The elders of Israel sat with Elisha.
The king of Israel sent a messenger to Elisha.
Before the messenger arrived, Elisha spoke to the elders.
Elisha said, “Do you see what is happening?”
Elisha called the king “this son of a murderer.”
Elisha said, “He has sent someone to take off my head.”
Elisha told the elders, “When the messenger comes, close the door.”
Elisha said, “Press the messenger against the door to keep him out.”
Elisha asked, “Do you not hear the sound of his master’s feet coming after him?”
passages.original: וֶאֱלִישָׁע֙ יֹשֵׁ֣ב בְּבֵית֔וֹ וְהַזְּקֵנִ֖ים יֹשְׁבִ֣ים אִתּ֑וֹ וַיִּשְׁלַ֨ח אִ֜ישׁ מִלְּפָנָ֗יו בְּטֶ֣רֶם יָבֹא֩ הַמַּלְאָ֨ךְ אֵלָ֜יו וְה֣וּא׀ אָמַ֣ר אֶל־ הַזְּקֵנִ֗ים הַרְּאִיתֶם֙ כִּֽי־ שָׁלַ֞ח בֶּן־ הַֽמְרַצֵּ֤חַ הַזֶּה֙ לְהָסִ֣יר אֶת־ רֹאשִׁ֔י רְא֣וּ׀ כְּבֹ֣א הַמַּלְאָ֗ךְ סִגְר֤וּ הַדֶּ֙לֶת֙ וּלְחַצְתֶּ֤ם אֹתוֹ֙ בַּדֶּ֔לֶת הֲל֗וֹא ק֛וֹל רַגְלֵ֥י אֲדֹנָ֖יו אַחֲרָֽיו׃

passages.text: While Elisha was still speaking with them, the messenger came down to him. And the king said, “This calamity is from the LORD. Why should I wait for the LORD any longer?”
passages.sermon:
Elisha was a prophet of God.
Elisha was still speaking with the elders.
A messenger arrived at Elisha’s house.
The king sent this messenger.
The king said, “This disaster comes from the LORD.”
The king said, “Why should I wait for the LORD any longer?”
passages.original: עוֹדֶ֙נּוּ֙ מְדַבֵּ֣ר עִמָּ֔ם וְהִנֵּ֥ה הַמַּלְאָ֖ךְ יֹרֵ֣ד אֵלָ֑יו וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הִנֵּֽה־ זֹ֤את הָֽרָעָה֙ מֵאֵ֣ת יְהוָ֔ה מָֽה־ אוֹחִ֥יל לַיהוָ֖ה עֽוֹד׃ס
